solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Set down soldiers, infantry principally, in training camp (7)

indicators.note: 'principally' means chiefly, first of all, so it takes the first letter of each of soldiers and infantry
'in' places those two letters inside the camp's name

blocks.note: a depot is a military training base
first letters of soldiers and infantry

annotation.surface: Troops being dropped off at a training camp.
annotation.walkthrough: "Principally" covers both soldiers and infantry, not infantry alone, so the insert is two initials rather than a word for soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set something down on a surface is to deposit it.

entries.clue: Submissive medic on French island (6)

annotation.surface: A meek doctor posted to an island in France.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue "on" means placed after: the island sits below the medic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a docile person does as they are told, which is to be submissive.

entries.clue: Church leader perturbed at first about petty quarrel (7)

indicators.note: 'at first' means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of perturbed is used

blocks.note: a tiff is a minor squabble

annotation.surface: A bishop rattled by a minor spat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Perturbed" looks like an anagram signal, but "at first" claims it: only its initial is used.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pontiff is the usual title for the Pope, head of the Roman Catholic Church.

entries.clue: Way a person cut a flowering plant (9)

blocks.note: one = a person, as in 'one never knows'
to crop is to cut short

annotation.surface: Someone trimming a plant beside the path.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cut" reads as a verb acting on the plant; it is just another piece of the charade.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: stonecrop, or sedum, is a low succulent that bears small starry flowers.

entries.clue: New term mother engendered primarily for temperature gauge (11)

indicators.note: 'new' means made afresh, so the letters of term mother are remade in a fresh order
'primarily' means in the first place, so it takes the first letter of engendered

blocks.note: first letter of engendered, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A mother coining a fresh word for a measuring device.
annotation.walkthrough: The E from engendered joins the ten letters of term mother before the shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a thermometer is the instrument that gauges, or measures, temperature.

entries.clue: Greek god’s verbal plea for support? (7)

indicators.note: 'verbal' means spoken, so the plea is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a call for others to support us

annotation.surface: A god calling out for backing.
annotation.walkthrough: Bacchus is better known as the Roman name, but the Greeks also used it for Dionysus, so the definition is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Bacchus, the god of wine, is a Greek god, another name for Dionysus.

entries.clue: Extra purchase, by the sound of it (3)

indicators.note: 'by the sound of it' means judging by how it sounds, so the word is heard rather than seen

annotation.surface: An additional item bought.
annotation.walkthrough: "Extra" looks like an adjective for the purchase; it is a cricket noun. In cricket a bye is a run scored without the ball touching the bat.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket sense: byes are counted among the extras, runs not credited to any batsman.

entries.clue: Prickly plants originally culled before opening of play (5)

indicators.note: 'originally' means at the origin, so it takes the first letter of culled
'before' puts that letter ahead of the rest

blocks.note: Act I is how a play opens

annotation.surface: Spiky plants weeded out before the curtain goes up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Opening of play" tempts you to take P; it is the play's first act, ACT I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: cacti are the spiny succulents, so prickly plants.

entries.clue: Non-believing female overcome by high temperature (7)

indicators.note: 'overcome by' means lying beneath, so in a down clue the female sits under the temperature

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird

annotation.surface: A sceptical woman laid low by a fever.
annotation.walkthrough: "Overcome" suggests defeat, but in a down clue it is only placement: the hen comes below the heat.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjectival use: heathen describes someone holding no, or the wrong, religious belief.

entries.clue: Day Moses exercised spitz-like dogs (8)

indicators.note: 'exercised' means put through its paces, so the letters are moved about

annotation.surface: A man called Moses walking the dogs one day.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dog walk, which hides that the dogs are the answer and the walk is the shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: Samoyeds are fluffy white Siberian dogs of the spitz family.

entries.clue: Is one not able to meet south-east Asian citizens? (9)

blocks.note: can't one? = is one not able?

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about whether you can meet people from South-East Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: "South-east Asian" reads as one phrase; it splits into the compass point for the wordplay and Asian for the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: the Cantonese are the people of Canton, now Guangzhou, in southern China.

entries.clue: Appeal of Daily Mail, initially (5)

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so it takes the first letter of Mail

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, also called a char

annotation.surface: The attraction of a British tabloid newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British newspaper, but here the two words part: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: charm and appeal both name the quality that attracts people.

entries.clue: Folk traditions one stops in French department (5)

indicators.note: 'stops in' means stays inside, as a guest stops in a house, so the one sits inside the traditions

annotation.surface: Folk customs lingering in a region of France.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "stops in" as lingering in France; in the wordplay it is the one that stops inside the lore.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Loire is one of France's départements, the administrative areas, named after the river.

entries.clue: Sickeningly upset most of malt whisky (9)

indicators.note: 'upset' means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order
'most of' means all but a little, so malt loses its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone feeling ill after too much single malt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Most of" applies only to malt; the whisky stays whole.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: mawkishly means in a cloying, sentimental way, sweet enough to sicken.

entries.clue: Around noon, preacher finally consumed beer and cheese (11)

indicators.note: 'around' means surrounding, so the preacher's name wraps round the noon
'finally' means at the end, so it takes the last letter of consumed

annotation.surface: A clergyman's midday lunch of a pint and some cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: "Around noon" reads as a time of day; it tells you the preacher goes around the N. Wesley is the preacher crosswords reach for.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Wensleydale is a crumbly white cheese from the Yorkshire dale of that name.

entries.clue: Supervisors inspired by alternative idea not referred to previously (14)

indicators.note: 'inspired' means breathed in, so the supervisors are drawn inside the other letters
'alternative' means another version, so idea not comes in another order

annotation.surface: Bosses stirred by a different notion.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not" looks like it negates the definition, but it belongs to the anagram fodder with idea.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: aforementioned describes something already mentioned, referred to earlier.

entries.clue: Thoroughgoing quartet entering in future, perhaps (9)

indicators.note: 'entering' means going into, so the quartet goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: the future is one tense of a verb; 'perhaps' marks an example

annotation.surface: A string quartet rehearsing hard for what lies ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: "Future, perhaps" is grammar, not time: future is one example of a tense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an intensive effort is thoroughgoing, concentrated and complete.

entries.clue: Old German’s afterthought about game Welsh girl (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the afterthought goes round the game

blocks.note: a postscript, added after a letter
Siân is a Welsh girl's name

annotation.surface: A German's postscript about a sport and a girl from Wales.
annotation.walkthrough: "Game" is rugby union by its initials, a standing crossword abbreviation; Siân is a common name in Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: Prussia was a German kingdom that no longer exists, so a Prussian is a German of old.

entries.clue: Summing-up of surrender by army corps (14)

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

annotation.surface: A report on an army unit's surrender.
annotation.walkthrough: "By" places the surrender beside the corps; in the answer the corps comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a recapitulation restates the main points, which is a summing-up.

entries.clue: US partnership in Civil Service, a cause of much amusement (7)

indicators.note: 'in' means inside, so the amusing thing sits within CS

blocks.note: the initial letters of Civil Service
a hoot is something very funny

annotation.surface: An American joint venture with the civil service turning out to be hilarious.
annotation.walkthrough: The British Civil Service is the permanent staff of government departments; here it just supplies its initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: cahoots, American in origin, is partnership, usually of a shady kind, as in 'in cahoots'.

entries.clue: Indirect learning ability encountered in old varsity sportsperson (7)

indicators.note: 'encountered in' means met inside, so the ability is found within the sportsperson

blocks.note: a Blue has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport

annotation.surface: A former university athlete who is bright but roundabout.
annotation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is awarded for representing the university against the other in a sport.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an oblique remark comes at its point sideways, which is indirect.

entries.clue: Fashionable group taking in start of county cricket, say? (6)

indicators.note: 'taking in' means admitting inside, so the group holds the letter
'start of' means the beginning, so it takes the first letter of county

annotation.surface: A smart crowd at a county cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: County cricket is Britain's first-class competition, but the cricket here is the chirping creature; "say" signals an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a cricket is one kind of insect.

entries.clue: Academic canny concealing report of arrest? (9)

indicators.note: 'concealing' means hiding, so canny holds the sound inside it
a report is something heard, so the word for arrest is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to collar someone is to arrest them

annotation.surface: A sharp-witted scholar hiding news of a police arrest.
annotation.walkthrough: "Report" looks like a news story; it is the sound of collar, respelt to fit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scholarly and academic both describe learned, university-style work.

entries.clue: Counsel possibly ignoring wife’s thickness (5)

indicators.note: 'ignoring' means paying no attention to, so the lawyer goes on without the wife's W

blocks.note: counsel is one kind of lawyer

annotation.surface: A barrister overlooking a spouse's stupidity.
annotation.walkthrough: "Thickness" looks like dimness to go with the lawyer; it is a thickness of material, as of paint.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a layer is one thickness, as in a single coat of paint.

entries.clue: Yarn assimilated by many Londoners (5)

indicators.note: 'assimilated by' means absorbed into, so the answer is absorbed inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A tale taken up by lots of Londoners.
annotation.walkthrough: "Yarn" suggests a story that Londoners pass round; here it is thread.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: nylon is a synthetic fibre spun into yarn.

entries.clue: Like heavy metal? That’s mild sarcasm (5)

blocks.note: resembling a dense metal used for tools, with -Y added
gentle mockery by saying the opposite

annotation.surface: A rock fan's remark greeted as sarcasm.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is a jokey coinage, IRON plus -Y, like iron; the second is the everyday word.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: irony-as-iron-like fits a heavy metal, and irony, saying the opposite of what you mean, is a mild sarcasm.

entries.clue: Female slave’s poem involving wild quails (9)

indicators.note: 'involving' means wrapping in, so the poem wraps round the rest
'wild' means unruly, so the letters of quails run free in a new order

annotation.surface: A poem about a slave girl that features game birds.
annotation.walkthrough: "Quails" can be a verb, to cower, which suits a slave; here it is only letters to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: an odalisque was a female slave or concubine in an Ottoman harem.

entries.clue: Physicist’s residence in Bow, do we hear? (3)

indicators.note: 'do we hear' asks us to listen, so the answer is the sound of the words

blocks.note: home, as said by a Cockney who drops the H

annotation.surface: A scientist's house in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops H, so home becomes 'ome.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: Georg Ohm was the German physicist whose name became the unit of resistance.

entries.clue: Time relative backed strange patent medicine (7)

indicators.note: 'backed' means moved backwards, so time and relative are turned round

annotation.surface: A family member putting money on a dubious remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: "Backed" reads as betting on the medicine; it turns T and SON round.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a nostrum is a quack remedy sold on its maker's claims, like a patent medicine.

entries.clue: Young hare heading off round back of this mountain (7)

indicators.note: 'heading off' means the head goes off, so the first letter is dropped
'round' means encircling, so the shortened hare goes round the letter
'back of' means the rear, so it takes the last letter of this

annotation.surface: A baby hare running off round a peak.
annotation.walkthrough: A leveret is a hare in its first year. "This" does double duty, supplying its last letter and pointing at the mountain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by reference: 'this mountain' points to the answer itself, and Everest is the world's highest mountain.
